docs.title: HostLocal developer docs
docs.text: HostLocal is an Android app (Kotlin, Jetpack Compose) that serves one folder of videos from a phone, read-only, to other devices on the same network. The main use is a TV connected to the phone's mobile hotspot, playing videos in VLC without copying files. Phone and TV can instead share a home router.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text:
• FTP: anonymous, read-only, on port 2121. VLC connects with ftp://<phone-ip>:2121/.
  • hostlocal.local: a stable name for the phone, advertised with mDNS, so users don't type a changing IP on laptops.
  • DLNA / UPnP: VLC lists the phone under Local Network, with thumbnails, without typing anything.
  • Follows the network: serves on the hotspot address if the hotspot is on, otherwise the Wi-Fi address, and rebinds when it changes.

docs.title: Tech at a glance
docs.text: Area Choice Language / UI Kotlin 2.0.21, Jetpack Compose (Material 3) Build Gradle 8.10.2, Android Gradle Plugin 8.7.3, JDK 17 SDK minSdk 26, targetSdk 33, compileSdk 36 FTP Apache MINA FtpServer 1.2.0 mDNS JmDNS 3.5.9 DLNA HTTP NanoHTTPD 2.3.1; UPnP/SSDP code written in-repo Tests JUnit 4 on the JVM (no emulator needed)

docs.title: The one thing to know first
docs.text: Discovery is the hard part, not serving files. Serving over FTP and HTTP is plain and works everywhere. Whether another device finds the phone depends on multicast traffic, which Android clients, routers and Wi-Fi chips treat inconsistently. Read How devices find the phone before changing anything in Ssdp.kt or MdnsHost.kt.

docs.title: Architecture overview
docs.text:
One foreground service owns three servers. A watcher inside the service decides which network address to serve on, and starts or restarts the servers whenever that changes.

flowchart TB
    UI[MainActivity<br/>Compose UI] -- start/stop --> SVC[HostService<br/>foreground service]
    UI -. polls every 2s .-> ST[(Static status<br/>in HostService / SsdpStats)]

    SVC --> W[Watcher thread<br/>every 3 s]
    W --> HS[Hotspot.currentAddress]
    HS -- IPv4 or null --> W

    W --> FTP[FtpHost<br/>MINA, port 2121]
    W --> MDNS[MdnsHost<br/>JmDNS, hostlocal.local]
    W --> DLNA[DlnaHost]

    DLNA --> HTTP[DlnaServer<br/>NanoHTTPD, port 8200]
    DLNA --> SSDP[SsdpAdvertiser<br/>UDP 1900]
    HTTP --> CD[DlnaContent / DidlBuilder<br/>browse + ids]
    HTTP --> TH[VideoThumbs]
    FTP --> FS[(Shared folder)]
    HTTP --> FS

docs.title: Request flow
docs.text:
1. The user taps Start. MainActivity calls HostService.start(), which starts a foreground service.
  2. HostService.onStartCommand checks the shared folder exists, takes the Wi-Fi, multicast and wake locks, and starts the watcher.
  3. Every 3 seconds the watcher calls Hotspot.currentAddress(). If the address changed, all servers stop and boundIp is updated.
  4. For the current address, any server that is not running is started: FTP, mDNS, DLNA. Each retries on its own, so one failure doesn't restart the others.
  5. The UI reads static status fields (HostService.ftpAddress, SsdpStats, ...) every 2 seconds and redraws.

docs.title: Key properties
docs.text:
• Everything binds to one IP. FTP and DLNA bind to the chosen interface address, not 0.0.0.0, so nothing is exposed on mobile data.
  • Read-only. FTP user has no write authority; DLNA only serves GET requests for video files under the root.
  • No persistent state besides the folder path and a generated DLNA UUID (SharedPreferences).
  • Status is process-global. The UI and service share state through @Volatile fields on companion objects. That is simple and fine for a single service, but it means there is exactly one server set per process.

docs.title: Threads
docs.text:
Thread Owner Work Main Android Compose UI, service callbacks pool-* (single) HostService The 3-second watcher; starts and stops servers MINA threads FtpHost FTP sessions NanoHTTPD threads DlnaServer One per HTTP connection, including media streaming ssdp-listen SsdpAdvertiser Blocks on UDP 1900, answers searches pool-* (single) SsdpAdvertiser Announcements every 60 s JmDNS threads MdnsHost mDNS responder Cleanup executor HostService.onDestroy Stops servers off the main thread

Warning

stopServers() does network I/O. Never call it on the main thread.

docs.title: Workflow
docs.text:
1. Branch from main. Prefix with your handle (the maintainer uses shubh/), e.g. shubh/fix-oneplus-hotspot-iface.
  2. Make a focused change with tests.
  3. Run ./gradlew testDebugUnitTest assembleDebug and, for UI or service changes, smoke test on a device or emulator (Testing).
  4. Run mkdocs build --strict if you touched docs.
  5. Open a PR with what changed, why, and how you tested it. Say explicitly if you could not test on real hardware.

docs.title: Commit messages
docs.text:
Short imperative subject (about 70 characters), blank line, then a body explaining the why. History reads like:

Serve on router Wi-Fi when no hotspot is active

Previously only hotspot interfaces were used. Now FTP and mDNS bind to
the hotspot IP if present, else wlan0/eth IP...

docs.title: Code style
docs.text:
• Kotlin official style (kotlin.code.style=official). Match the surrounding code.
  • Keep comments to the why: constraints, platform quirks, security boundaries. Don't narrate the code.
  • Put logic in plain Kotlin that can be tested on the JVM; keep Android-specific code thin.
  • Anything touching the network must run off the main thread.

docs.title: Where to be careful
docs.text: Area Rule DlnaContent.resolve Security boundary. Any change needs path-traversal tests. FTP authorities Read-only is a product promise. Don't add write permissions casually. Binding Servers bind to the chosen interface IP, never 0.0.0.0. HostService.syncToHotspot Servers retry independently; keep that. Discovery code Test on a real hotspot and a router; the emulator can't show multicast behaviour. Release config R8 stays off unless MINA and JmDNS are re-verified on a device.

docs.title: Common tasks
docs.text:
Support a new video format

Add the extension and MIME type to DlnaContent.VIDEO_MIME. FTP serves any file already. Add a test case in DlnaTest.

Support a new phone's hotspot interface

Add its name to Hotspot.AP_NAME and a case to HotspotTest.

Change a port

Edit the constant in Settings.kt. Update Reference and any firewall notes. Tests use their own ports.

Add a setting

Add a property in Settings.kt, a control in MainActivity.kt, and document the key in UI and settings.

docs.title: Secrets
docs.text: Never commit keystore.properties, *.jks or local.properties (all gitignored). Don't add credentials or analytics.

docs.title: Docs
docs.text: Docs live in docs/, nav in mkdocs.yml. Update the relevant page when behaviour changes, and add new pages to nav (strict mode fails on pages not linked and on broken links).

docs.title: Docs publishing
docs.text:
.github/workflows/docs.yml builds the site with mkdocs build --strict on every PR that touches docs/, mkdocs.yml or requirements-docs.txt. On a push to main it also publishes the built site to the build branch (mkdocs gh-deploy --force --remote-branch build). That branch contains generated files only; never edit it by hand.

To serve it, in the GitHub repo go to Settings → Pages → Source: Deploy from a branch → Branch build, folder / (root). The workflow needs contents: write, which the workflow file already requests.

docs.title: Design decisions
docs.text: Short records of why things are the way they are. Change them deliberately.

docs.title: Native Android, Kotlin
docs.text: The app needs a foreground service, hotspot interface detection, multicast locks and raw sockets. Native Kotlin with Compose gives direct access; cross-platform frameworks would still need native modules. iOS is out of scope: it can't run a background FTP server reliably.

docs.title: FTP with Apache MINA
docs.text: Chosen for a mature server with a read-only permission model. Requires real file paths (see below). Port 2121 because ports under 1024 need root. Anonymous and read-only so a TV needs no setup; the hotspot password is the gate.

docs.title: Storage: all-files access
docs.text:
MINA serves a java.io.File root, and the DLNA server streams files with FileInputStream. Storage Access Framework URIs don't give that. The app therefore uses MANAGE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE ("All files access"), and the SAF picker is used only to pick a folder, converted to a path by treeUriToPath.

Trade-off: this permission is restricted on Google Play. It is fine for side-loading and personal use. A Play release would need a SAF-based FileSystemView and DocumentFile streaming, which is a rewrite of both servers' file access.

docs.title: mDNS with JmDNS, not NsdManager
docs.text: NsdManager registers services but doesn't answer A queries for an arbitrary hostname. JmDNS runs a real responder, so hostlocal.local resolves. It must be bound to the chosen interface address.

docs.title: Hand-written UPnP, not Cling or jUPnP
docs.text: A video-only MediaServer needs SSDP, one SOAP service and file streaming, around 500 lines. Cling is unmaintained and jUPnP pulls in Jetty. Writing it also keeps SSDP behaviour under our control, which mattered while debugging discovery.

docs.title: DLNA added beside FTP, not instead of it
docs.text: Android clients can't resolve hostlocal.local, so DLNA gives zero-typing discovery. FTP stays because it works reliably when discovery doesn't (manual entry). An SMB server was considered and rejected: it needs port 445 (root) and there is no suitable maintained library.

docs.title: Stateless DLNA object ids
docs.text: Base64 of the relative path avoids a database or in-memory table and survives restarts. The cost is that ids reveal paths to clients, which already see them.

docs.title: Polling watcher, not network callbacks
docs.text: A 3-second poll of NetworkInterface is simple and robust across OEM hotspot implementations, where ConnectivityManager callbacks don't reliably report the tethering interface. Cost: up to 3 seconds to notice a change.

docs.title: Bind to the interface IP
docs.text: FTP and DLNA never listen on 0.0.0.0, so they aren't reachable over mobile data or other interfaces.

docs.title: R8 off
docs.text: MINA and JmDNS use reflection. Shrinking saves little (the APK is about 7 MB) and risks runtime failures that only appear on a device.

docs.title: Unicast, broadcast and multicast announcements
docs.text: Added to cope with routers that filter multicast. It didn't make VLC list the server on the test router, but it is cheap and kept. See Networking.

Tool Version Notes JDK 17 The Android Gradle Plugin 8.7 needs 17. JDK 11 will not work. Android SDK platform 36, build-tools 35+ Install with Android Studio or sdkmanager. adb any recent Part of platform-tools. Device Android 8.0+ (API 26) The author's phone runs Android 13 (OxygenOS 13).

Point Gradle at the SDK with local.properties in the repo root (Android Studio writes this for you; the file is gitignored):

docs.title: Build and install
docs.text:
./gradlew assembleDebug
adb install -r app/build/outputs/apk/debug/app-debug.apk

Run the unit tests (JVM, no device):

./gradlew testDebugUnitTest
If ./gradlew can't download Gradle

On some networks Java's connection to the Gradle download times out while curl works. Download the zip yourself and run that Gradle directly:

curl -L -o gradle-8.10.2-bin.zip https://services.gradle.org/distributions/gradle-8.10.2-bin.zip
unzip gradle-8.10.2-bin.zip -d ~/gradle
~/gradle/gradle-8.10.2/bin/gradle assembleDebug

Or open the project in Android Studio, which manages Gradle itself.

docs.title: First run on a device
docs.text:
1. Open HostLocal. A Setup checklist lists what is missing:
    • All-files access: needed to read videos with real file paths (see decisions).
    • Notifications: for the foreground-service notification (Android 13+).
    • Battery optimization: recommended, so the server survives with the screen off.
  2. Choose the folder to share (default /storage/emulated/0/Movies).
  3. Turn on the hotspot, or join a Wi-Fi network.
  4. Tap Start. The screen shows ftp://<ip>:2121 and the status of each server.

docs.title: Release build and signing
docs.text:
The release build is signed only if keystore.properties exists in the repo root (gitignored, as is *.jks):

storeFile=/absolute/path/to/release.jks
storePassword=...
keyAlias=hostlocal
keyPassword=...

keytool -genkeypair -keystore ~/.hostlocal/release.jks -alias hostlocal \
  -keyalg RSA -keysize 2048 -validity 10000
./gradlew assembleRelease
$ANDROID_HOME/build-tools/36.0.0/apksigner verify --print-certs app/build/outputs/apk/release/app-release.apk

Back up the keystore

If the signing key is lost, a new APK can't be installed over the old one. Keep the keystore and keystore.properties somewhere safe and out of git.

Without keystore.properties, assembleRelease still builds, but the APK is unsigned and can't be installed.

R8 minification is off on purpose: MINA and JmDNS rely on reflection. Don't enable it without testing both servers on a device.

docs.title: Building the docs
docs.text:
python3 -m venv .venv-docs && source .venv-docs/bin/activate
pip install -r requirements-docs.txt
mkdocs serve          # live preview at http://127.0.0.1:8000
mkdocs build --strict # what CI should run; fails on broken links

docs.title: How devices find the phone
docs.text: Serving files is easy. Getting another device to find the phone is where this project spent most of its effort. Read this page before touching discovery code.

docs.title: Three ways in, three different mechanisms
docs.text: Method Mechanism Works on Type the IP none everything, always ftp://hostlocal.local:2121 mDNS multicast (UDP 5353) laptops. Not Android apps VLC → Local Network → HostLocal SSDP multicast (UDP 1900) depends on the network

docs.title: Observed results
docs.text: Setup Result Laptop, ping hostlocal.local works VLC on the phone itself (loopback) lists HostLocal as UPnP and FTP Tablet and Sony Bravia (VLC 3.7.1) on the phone's hotspot HostLocal listed Tablet and Bravia on router Wi-Fi not listed Same, with http://<phone-ip>:8200/desc.xml opened in a browser loads, so the network path exists Same, manual ftp://<phone-ip>:2121 in VLC works

docs.title: Why Android clients can't use hostlocal.local
docs.text: Android apps resolve names through the system resolver, which doesn't query mDNS for .local. VLC on Android therefore never asks the network. There is no app-side fix for the client. Options considered and rejected: a real domain with dynamic DNS (needs a domain and internet), running DNS on the phone (needs root; the hotspot's own DNS owns port 53).

docs.title: Why discovery fails on some Wi-Fi networks
docs.text:
VLC finds UPnP servers by multicasting a search to 239.255.255.250:1900 and waiting for replies. On the failing router the phone's SSDP counters stayed at 0 for other devices' searches, even though the TV and tablet were announcing on the network. So searches never arrived. Likely causes:

  • IGMP snooping or multicast filtering in the router or access point
  • client isolation / AP isolation (ruled out here, because HTTP between devices worked)
  • the phone's Wi-Fi chip dropping multicast (OxygenOS)

On the phone's own hotspot there is no router in the way and it works.

docs.title: What the app does about it
docs.text:
SsdpAdvertiser announces in three ways every 60 s: multicast, subnet broadcast, and unicast to every host. The goal was to reach clients even if multicast is filtered. On the test router this did not make VLC list the server: VLC only lists servers that answered its own search, and its search never reached the phone. The extra announcements are harmless and may help other clients.

The phone also holds a MulticastLock and a WifiLock (see Service). Those fix the phone's own receive filtering where the OEM honours them.

docs.title: Recommendations to users
docs.text:
1. Prefer the hotspot: no router, discovery works.
  2. On router Wi-Fi: add ftp://<phone-ip>:2121 once in VLC (Browse → Add server). Reserve the phone's IP in the router (DHCP reservation) so it never changes.
  3. If you control the router: disable IGMP snooping / multicast filtering for Wi-Fi.

docs.title: Done
docs.text: Milestone Summary M0 Project scaffold, foreground service skeleton M1 Anonymous read-only FTP on 2121 M2 Hotspot IP detection, folder picker, live status M3 mDNS hostlocal.local + _ftp._tcp (JmDNS) M4 Hardening: rebind on network change, locks, battery prompt, per-server retry M5 Setup checklist, icon, signed release config M6 DLNA/UPnP server with thumbnails; serves on router Wi-Fi when no hotspot

docs.title: Known limitations
docs.text:
• Discovery on router Wi-Fi is unreliable: VLC on a tablet and a Sony Bravia (VLC 3.7.1) did not list the server, while the hotspot works. Root cause is multicast not reaching the phone on that router. See Networking.
  • hostlocal.local does not resolve on Android clients.
  • Not verified on hardware: playback of a real 4K file over Wi-Fi, non-primary storage volumes, behaviour after many hours with the screen off.
  • All-files access blocks a Play Store release as-is (decision).
  • Hotspot interface names are matched from a list; an unknown OEM name shows "No network".
  • Status is held in static fields, so there is one server set per process and the UI polls instead of observing.
  • No UI tests and no app CI (only docs CI).
  • Only IPv4.

docs.title: Ideas
docs.text: Idea Notes Cast to TV The phone scans the subnet by unicast M-SEARCH, finds DLNA renderers (a Bravia is one), and sends SetAVTransportURI + Play with a /media/... URL. Works where multicast is filtered. Plays in the TV's own player, not VLC. Optional FTP login Username/password for non-hotspot networks Multiple folders Several roots under one login SAF-based file access Remove MANAGE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE, enable Play distribution Observable state Replace static fields and polling with a bound service or StateFlow Eventing / SUBSCRIBE Only if a client needs it CI Run testDebugUnitTest, assembleDebug and mkdocs build --strict on PRs Auto-start on hotspot Start the service when tethering turns on

docs.title: Rejected
docs.text: Idea Why Real domain + dynamic DNS Needs a domain and internet; the product is offline-first DNS server on the phone Needs root; system owns port 53 on the hotspot SMB server Needs port 445 (root); no suitable maintained library Spoofing DNS replies Needs root, and it is unsafe

docs.title: Testing
docs.text: Three levels: JVM unit tests (fast, run these always), emulator smoke tests, and real-device checks (the only way to verify discovery).

docs.title: Unit tests
docs.text:
./gradlew testDebugUnitTest

Reports: app/build/reports/tests/testDebugUnitTest/index.html.

File Covers HotspotTest Interface choice: hotspot preferred, Wi-Fi fallback, mobile data ignored FtpHostTest Real MINA server on 127.0.0.1:2129: anonymous download works, upload and delete rejected DlnaTest Real HTTP server on 127.0.0.1:8209: descriptions, Browse and paging, Range 200/206/416, path traversal, hidden and non-video files, id round trip, SSDP matching, subnet sweep math

Fixed ports

The tests bind real ports (2129 and 8209). Don't run two Gradle test processes at once.

docs.title: Writing tests
docs.text:
• Keep new logic pure where possible, as Hotspot.pickAddress, SsdpMessages and DlnaContent.parseRange are. Android classes (Context, MediaMetadataRetriever) can't run in JVM tests, which is why DlnaServer takes a nullable ThumbProvider.
  • For server behaviour, start the server on 127.0.0.1 with a temp folder and talk to it over HTTP/FTP, as the existing tests do.

docs.title: Emulator smoke test
docs.text:
The emulator has a client network (eth0/wlan0, 10.0.2.x) but no hotspot and no multicast to your machine, so it verifies startup, not discovery.

./gradlew assembleDebug
adb install -r app/build/outputs/apk/debug/app-debug.apk
adb shell appops set com.hostlocal MANAGE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE allow
adb shell pm grant com.hostlocal android.permission.POST_NOTIFICATIONS
adb shell am start -n com.hostlocal/.MainActivity

The service isn't exported, so start it by tapping Start in the UI (or adb shell input tap). Then:

adb shell ss -ltn | grep -E ':(2121|8200)'     # both listening on 10.0.2.x
adb logcat -d | grep -c "FATAL EXCEPTION"      # expect 0

To reach the FTP server from your machine on the emulator, forward its ports (the server binds to the LAN IP, so test from inside with nc, or use a loopback-bound build). Unit tests already cover FTP behaviour.

docs.title: Real-device checklist
docs.text:
Do this before a release, on the phone hotspot and on a router.

  1. Install, grant setup items, pick a folder with a few videos, Start.
  2. Laptop: ping hostlocal.local; curl ftp://<ip>:2121/ lists videos; an upload is refused.
  3. VLC on the phone: Browse → Local Network shows HostLocal (UPnP, FTP).
  4. VLC on a TV/tablet: Local Network shows HostLocal. If not, ftp://<ip>:2121 added manually plays and seeks.
  5. Streaming: play a large (ideally 4K) file and seek.
  6. Network change: turn the hotspot off and on; the screen returns to "serving" with the new IP, and clients reconnect.
  7. Screen off for several minutes: playback continues.

docs.title: Discovery checks from a laptop
docs.text: See How to test discovery yourself for the SSDP search script, and use dns-sd -G v4 hostlocal.local for mDNS.

docs.title: What is not covered
docs.text: No UI tests. No test of real multicast across a router. No automated test of thumbnail generation on a real video. See Roadmap.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Likely cause What to do Screen says "No network - turn on hotspot or join Wi-Fi" while hotspot is on OEM hotspot interface name not in Hotspot.AP_NAME adb shell ip -4 -o addr with hotspot on; add the name and a test (Network selection) Start is greyed out All-files access not granted Tap the setup button, enable it, return to the app "Folder not found" on Start Path doesn't exist or no permission Fix the path or re-pick the folder Laptop resolves hostlocal.local, Android VLC doesn't Android doesn't do mDNS names Use the IP or DLNA (Networking) VLC lists the phone's own entry but not on the TV Multicast not delivered Try the hotspot; see below FTP connects but listing hangs Passive ports 50000-50010 blocked Allow them, or test on the hotspot FTP error: ... Address already in use Port 2121 held by an old process Stop the app, wait a few seconds, Start again DLNA error: ... Port 8200 or UDP 1900 in use Check what holds it; another UPnP app can hold 1900 Server stops with the screen off OEM kills the service Disable battery optimization; on OxygenOS also allow background activity No thumbnails Extraction failed for that file Expected for odd codecs; browsing still works

docs.title: Reading the status block
docs.text:
• FTP: serving on <ip> / mDNS: advertising hostlocal.local / DLNA: serving as HostLocal: each server is up. waiting for network means no usable address.
  • SSDP searches seen: N, answered: M (last from IP): searches that reached the phone. 0 from other devices means multicast isn't arriving.
  • SSDP packets by sender: every datagram on UDP 1900 by sender IP. Smart TVs normally announce constantly; if only the phone's own IP appears, the network or the phone's chip is dropping multicast.

docs.title: Useful commands
docs.text:
adb shell dumpsys wifi | grep -i -E "WifiLock|Multicaster"   # are the locks held?
adb shell ss -ltn | grep -E ':(2121|8200)'                   # are servers listening?
adb logcat | grep -E "hostlocal|FATAL"
curl ftp://<phone-ip>:2121/                                  # list the shared folder
curl -r 0-99 -i http://<phone-ip>:8200/media/<id>.mp4        # expect 206

docs.title: DLNA / UPnP
docs.text:
Source: app/src/main/java/com/hostlocal/dlna/, tests: DlnaTest.kt

A minimal UPnP MediaServer:1 so VLC lists the phone under Local Network without typing a name or IP. It is hand-written (no Cling or jUPnP) because the client only needs three small pieces.

docs.title: Pieces
docs.text: Piece File Job SSDP discovery Ssdp.kt Answer M-SEARCH, announce NOTIFY alive/byebye Device and service XML DlnaDescriptions.kt /desc.xml, /cd/scpd.xml, /cm/scpd.xml ContentDirectory + streaming DlnaServer.kt, DlnaContent.kt SOAP Browse, DIDL-Lite, Range streaming Wiring DlnaHost.kt Starts HTTP then SSDP; stops both

docs.title: HTTP routes (port 8200)
docs.text:
Route Purpose GET /desc.xml Device description (urn:schemas-upnp-org:device:MediaServer:1, friendly name "HostLocal") GET /cd/scpd.xml, /cm/scpd.xml Service descriptions POST /cd/control SOAP: Browse, GetSystemUpdateID, GetSearchCapabilities, GetSortCapabilities POST /cm/control SOAP: GetProtocolInfo, GetCurrentConnectionIDs, GetCurrentConnectionInfo GET /media/<id>.<ext> Video bytes with Range support GET /thumb/<id>.jpg JPEG thumbnail

Eventing (SUBSCRIBE) is not implemented; VLC doesn't need it.

docs.title: Object ids
docs.text:
An id is the URL-safe base64 of the path relative to the shared root (0 for the root). It is stateless and reversible: no table to keep in sync, and ids stay stable across restarts.

DlnaContent.resolve(root, id) is the security boundary. It returns a file only if:

  • the id decodes, and no path segment starts with . (blocks .. and hidden files),
  • the canonical path is inside the canonical root (blocks symlink escapes),
  • the file exists.

media and thumb also require a known video extension. Tests: traversalRejected, nonVideoNotServed.

docs.title: Browse
docs.text:
DidlBuilder.browse(objectId, flag, start, count) returns a DIDL-Lite document plus NumberReturned and TotalMatches.

  • BrowseDirectChildren pages with StartingIndex / RequestedCount (0 means all).
  • BrowseMetadata describes one object.
  • Folders sort first, then names case-insensitively. Hidden entries and non-video files are skipped.
  • Video extensions and MIME types live in DlnaContent.VIDEO_MIME. Add a row to support a container.

docs.title: Streaming
docs.text:
DlnaServer.media serves straight from disk with a FileInputStream, positioned for Range:

  • no Range → 200, full length
  • valid range → 206 with Content-Range
  • unsatisfiable → 416
  • always Accept-Ranges: bytes and DLNA headers (contentFeatures.dlna.org, transferMode.dlna.org: Streaming)

No transcoding. The pure function DlnaContent.parseRange is unit-tested.

Throughput

A local download measured about 400 MB/s, so the server is not a bottleneck. Real limits are Wi-Fi airtime and the phone's storage. HTTP and FTP move the same bytes.

docs.title: Thumbnails
docs.text: VideoThumbs (Android) implements the ThumbProvider interface: MediaMetadataRetriever grabs a frame at about 1 s, scales to 320 px wide, writes a JPEG into cacheDir/thumbs, keyed by SHA-1 of path and mtime. A Semaphore(2) limits concurrent extraction. Failure returns null and the route 404s, so a missing thumbnail never breaks browsing. DlnaServer takes the provider as a nullable parameter so tests run on the JVM without Android.

docs.title: SSDP
docs.text:
SsdpMessages is pure (strings in, strings out) and unit-tested. SsdpAdvertiser:

  1. Binds a MulticastSocket to UDP 1900 (reuse-address), joins 239.255.255.250 on the interface that owns the bound IP.
  2. A listener thread answers matching M-SEARCH requests by unicast to the sender. It matches ssdp:all, upnp:rootdevice, the uuid:, the device type and both service types.
  3. Every 60 seconds it announces NOTIFY ssdp:alive three ways: to the multicast group, to the subnet broadcast address, and by unicast to every host in the subnet (SsdpMessages.hostsIn, capped at about 1,000 hosts). The last two exist for networks that filter multicast; see Networking.
  4. On stop it sends byebye, then closes the socket.

The device UUID is generated once and stored (Settings.dlnaUuid) so clients don't see a new server on every launch.

docs.title: Diagnostics
docs.text: SsdpStats (global object) counts searches received, replies sent, the last sender, and datagrams per sender IP. The main screen shows them. They answer the key question "do other devices' searches reach the phone at all?"

docs.title: Extending
docs.text:
• New action: add it to the when in contentDirectory() and to contentDirectoryScpd in DlnaDescriptions.kt.
  • Audio/images: widen children() and VIDEO_MIME, and set the right upnp:class in DidlBuilder.describe.
  • Always add a test in DlnaTest (the HTTP server runs on 127.0.0.1:8209 there).

docs.title: FTP server
docs.text:
Source: FtpHost.kt, test: FtpHostTest.kt

Wraps Apache MINA FtpServer.

docs.title: Behaviour
docs.text:
• Port 2121 (unprivileged; port 21 needs root). Constant: Settings.FTP_PORT.
  • Bound to the address chosen by network selection.
  • Anonymous login only, one user anonymous whose home is the shared folder.
  • Read-only: the user is created with an empty authorities list, so MINA rejects STOR, DELE, RNFR, MKD and the rest. An upload returns 550, a delete 450.
  • Passive mode ports 50000-50010 (Settings.PASSIVE_PORTS). Clients open data connections here, so a firewall in between must allow them.

docs.title: Why these choices
docs.text: Anonymous and read-only because the hotspot is already password-protected and the goal is zero setup on a TV. If you add authentication, keep VLC's behaviour in mind: its "Add server" screen asks for a username, but many users leave it blank.

docs.title: Changing it
docs.text:
• Port: change Settings.FTP_PORT. The UI and the DLNA _ftp._tcp advertisement read the constant.
  • Write access: add WritePermission() to authorities. Update FtpHostTest.uploadDenied, which asserts the opposite.
  • Different root: FtpHost(rootDir, bindAddress, port); tests use 127.0.0.1 and port 2129.

docs.title: Test notes
docs.text: FtpHostTest starts a real server on 127.0.0.1:2129 and uses java.net.URL("ftp://..."). It checks anonymous download, upload rejection and that the file is intact. Don't run it in parallel with another process using port 2129.

docs.title: Gotchas
docs.text:
• MINA on Android needs META-INF excludes in packaging (already in app/build.gradle.kts), and slf4j-android for logging.
  • The shared folder is read with real file paths, which requires all-files access (decision).

docs.title: mDNS hostname
docs.text:
Source: MdnsHost.kt

Advertises hostlocal.local and a _ftp._tcp service using JmDNS, bound to the chosen address.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text:
• JmDNS.create(address, "hostlocal") makes JmDNS answer A queries for hostlocal.local. with the bound address. This is a hostname responder, which Android's own NsdManager can't do (it only registers services).
  • Registers _ftp._tcp.local. on port 2121, named "HostLocal". VLC's local-network browser can list this.
  • The hostname is fixed in MdnsHost.HOSTNAME.

docs.title: Who can resolve it
docs.text:
Client Resolves hostlocal.local? macOS, iOS, Windows 10+, Linux with Avahi yes Android apps (VLC on phone, tablet, Android TV) no: the Android resolver doesn't do mDNS names

So the name helps laptops only. Android clients use DLNA or the IP.

docs.title: Verifying on a laptop
docs.text:
ping hostlocal.local
dns-sd -G v4 hostlocal.local      # macOS

Verified

Running the same JmDNS calls on a Mac and resolving with ping and dns-sd worked. Resolution on Android clients was found not to work.

docs.title: Lifecycle
docs.text:
Created and closed by HostService.syncToHotspot / stopServers. stop() unregisters services before closing; it can block, so it runs off the main thread.

Requires the MulticastLock held by HostService.

docs.title: Network selection
docs.text:
Source: Hotspot.kt, test: HotspotTest.kt

The app must serve on whichever network the phone currently offers, and that changes (hotspot on/off, Wi-Fi joined). Hotspot.currentAddress() returns one IPv4 address, or null.

docs.title: Rules
docs.text:
1. Look at interfaces that are up and not loopback.
  2. Keep only site-local IPv4 addresses (10.x, 172.16-31.x, 192.168.x).
  3. Prefer an access-point interface: names matching ap*, swlan*, softap*, wlan1+ or rndis*.
  4. Otherwise fall back to the client network: wlan0 or ethN.
  5. Otherwise null. Mobile data (rmnet_*) is never used.

The hotspot wins over Wi-Fi, so if the phone has both, clients on the hotspot are served.

docs.title: Why a name list
docs.text:
Android gives no public API for "the hotspot's IP". Interface names vary by chipset and OEM, so the app matches known names. pickAddress is pure (takes IfaceInfo(name, ipv4)), which is what HotspotTest exercises.

Unknown OEM interface names

If the app says "No network" while the hotspot is on, the OEM probably uses a name that isn't in the list. Get it with adb shell ip -4 -o addr while the hotspot is on, then add it to AP_NAME and a test case.

docs.title: Hotspot vs router
docs.text: Hotspot Router Wi-Fi Phone's address usually fixed (e.g. 192.168.43.1) DHCP, can change; reserve it in the router Discovery works often fails; see Networking Needs internet no no

docs.title: Changing the rules
docs.text: Edit the two regexes and add a case to HotspotTest. Keep the preference order tested (hotspotPreferredOverWifi, fallsBackToRouterWifi).

docs.title: Service and lifecycle
docs.text:
Source: HostService.kt

HostService is a foreground service (type connectedDevice). It exists to keep the servers alive while the app is in the background, and to reconfigure them when the network changes.

docs.title: Start and stop
docs.text:
• HostService.start(context) / stop(context) are the only entry points. Stop sends ACTION_STOP; the service calls stopSelf().
  • onStartCommand runs startForeground first (required within seconds of startForegroundService), then validates the folder. A missing folder sets lastError and stops the service.
  • It returns START_STICKY, so Android restarts it if the process is killed. After a restart the intent is null, which the code treats as a normal start.
  • onDestroy cancels the watcher, releases the locks and stops the servers on a throwaway executor.

docs.title: Locks
docs.text:
Lock Why MulticastLock Without it, Android's Wi-Fi chip may drop incoming multicast (SSDP, mDNS). WifiLock (FULL_LOW_LATENCY on API 29+) Keeps Wi-Fi out of power-save so multicast and long streams aren't throttled. PARTIAL_WAKE_LOCK Keeps the CPU running with the screen off during playback.

All three are non-reference-counted and released in onDestroy.

docs.title: The watcher
docs.text:
startWatcher schedules syncToHotspot(folder) every 3 seconds on a single-thread executor.

ip = Hotspot.currentAddress()
if ip != boundIp:  stopServers(); boundIp = ip; clear errors
if ip == null:     return                    # "waiting for network"
if ftp  == null:   try start FtpHost         # each server retries alone
if mdns == null:   try start MdnsHost
if dlna == null:   try start DlnaHost

Because each block checks its own null, a persistent failure (for example the DLNA port already in use) is retried every 3 seconds without bouncing FTP or mDNS. The error stays visible in the UI until it clears.

docs.title: Shared status
docs.text:
Companion @Volatile fields expose state to the UI:

Field Meaning running Service started ftpAddress, mdnsAddress, dlnaAddress Address each server is bound to, or null ftpError, mdnsError, dlnaError Last start error per server lastError Fatal start error (e.g. folder not found)

SsdpStats (in dlna/Ssdp.kt) holds discovery counters; see DLNA.

docs.title: Adding a fourth server
docs.text:
1. Add a wrapper class with start() and stop().
  2. Add a var and a block in syncToHotspot, plus a line in stopServers.
  3. Add ...Address and ...Error fields to the companion object.
  4. Show it in MainActivity.

docs.title: UI and settings
docs.text: Source: MainActivity.kt, Settings.kt, FolderPaths.kt

docs.title: MainActivity
docs.text:
A single Compose screen. It owns no server logic; it only starts and stops HostService and displays state.

  • A LaunchedEffect loop runs every 2 seconds. It re-reads Hotspot.currentAddress() and the static status fields from HostService and SsdpStats into Compose state. A tick counter forces recomposition for non-state reads.
  • Setup checklist appears while a permission is missing: all-files access, notifications (API 33+), battery-optimization exemption. Each item disappears once granted; onResume re-checks.
  • Start is disabled until all-files access is granted.
  • The folder field is editable only while stopped.
  • The status block shows each server's bound address or error, plus SSDP counters.

docs.title: Folder picker
docs.text: ActivityResultContracts.OpenDocumentTree returns a SAF tree URI. treeUriToPath converts it to a path (primary:Movies → /storage/emulated/0/Movies, other volumes → /storage/<id>/...). This only works because the app has all-files access; see decisions. Non-primary volumes haven't been tested.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
SharedPreferences file hostlocal:

Key Type Meaning folder String Shared folder path (default /storage/emulated/0/Movies) dlna_uuid String Generated once; DLNA device id

Constants: FTP_PORT = 2121, PASSIVE_PORTS = "50000-50010", DLNA_PORT = 8200, DLNA_NAME = "HostLocal".

docs.title: Adding a status line
docs.text:
1. Expose the value as a @Volatile field (see Service).
  2. Copy it into a remember { mutableStateOf(...) } inside the LaunchedEffect loop.
  3. Render it in the if (running) block.
